meta: A poor family with a sick person in bed is visited by two people in Michael Sweerts's Visiting the Sick, 1646.
about: In an Italian house a poor family with a sick person in bed is visited by two people. An old woman and a child warm themselves at the hearth. The picture is one of a series on the seven works of mercy. Michael Sweerts painted it in 1646, and the Rijksmuseum bought it with support from its photo sales committee.

meta: The weeping Hagar looks sharply upward with her face in soft light in Gerbrand van den Eeckhout's painting of the early 1640s.
about: Hagar weeps with her face bathed in soft light, turning away from us and looking sharply upward. At his wife Sarah's request, Abraham reluctantly cast out the Egyptian slave-maid Hagar and the son she had borne him, Ishmael. They ran out of water in the desert of Beersheba. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout painted the scene in the early 1640s, and it is in the Getty.

meta: Cows and sheep by a pool, a goat at the bushes and a peasant woman with a donkey, painted by Pieter Gerardus van Os in 1806.
about: Beside a pool along a road stand a few cows and sheep, and at the right a goat eats from the bushes. A peasant woman comes along the road with a donkey. Pieter Gerardus van Os painted this landscape with cattle in 1806.

meta: A lady has her hair done by a hairdresser and a maid beside a lit lamp in Constantin Guys's Finishing the Toilet.
about: A lady in a full skirt, an apron and a cap sits in a chair by a table with a lighted lamp. A male hairdresser in a smock stands at the left and a maid behind her at the right, and both arrange her hair. Constantin Guys made the picture around 1840.

meta: A ceiling painting with putti and a goat in its corners, probably from the palace of the Frisian stadtholders in Leeuwarden, by Elias van Nijmegen.
about: This ornamental ceiling painting shows putti in the corners busy with branches and playing with a goat. It is half of a pair, and it probably comes from the palace of the Frisian stadtholders in Leeuwarden. Elias van Nijmegen painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1695.

meta: Millais's Isabella, from Boccaccio's story of Lisabetta and the pot of basil, his first Pre-Raphaelite painting, shown in 1849.
about: Isabella, also called Lorenzo and Isabella, was Millais's first exhibited work in the Pre-Raphaelite style, finished soon after the Brotherhood was formed in 1848. It was first shown at the Royal Academy in 1849 and is now in the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool. It illustrates an episode from Boccaccio's Decameron, the tale of Lisabetta and the pot of basil, which Keats reused in his poem Isabella, or the Pot of Basil.

meta: A mother at a table drinks from a glass with her child on her arm in Louis Bernard Coclers's painting of 1794.
about: A mother sits at a table with her child in her arm and drinks from a glass. A loaf, butter, cheese and a bottle stand on the table before her, and a hearth is at the right. Louis Bernard Coclers painted it in 1794.

meta: Caravaggio's Portrait of a Courtesan, painted in 1597 to 1599 and destroyed in Berlin in 1945, known only from photographs.
about: Caravaggio painted this portrait between 1597 and 1599. It has been suggested that it shows the courtesan Fillide Melandroni as the goddess Flora. The painting was destroyed in Berlin in 1945 and is known only from photographs. Earlier scholars read the flower pressed to her breast as orange blossom or bergamot, symbols of marriage and fidelity, and took the subject to be Caterina Campi, Caravaggio's wife.

meta: A duck and a partridge with hunting gear on a stone plinth in Melchior d'Hondecoeter's A Hunter's Bag, about 1660.
about: A duck and a partridge lie on a stone plinth with hunting gear. Melchior d'Hondecoeter painted A Hunter's Bag, which the catalog dates to 1660. Mr. and Mrs. Kessler-Hülsmann of Kapelle op den Bosch gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Musicians with trumpets and flutes, studies by Raimundo de Madrazo for The Return of Christopher Columbus to the Spanish Court.
about: These are two studies made for the painting The Return of Christopher Columbus to the Spanish Court, which the Italian Charities of America own. The main group shows male musicians playing trumpets and flutes, and a second group at the bottom center of the sheet shows a single trumpeter. Raimundo de Madrazo made them.

meta: Satyrs spy on nymphs resting after a bath in Cornelis van Poelenburch's painting of 1627.
about: In a hilly landscape, a group of nude women rest beside a small lake after bathing. At the left satyrs come out from behind the rocks, and a group of women flee from them with raised arms. Cornelis van Poelenburch painted the picture in 1627.

meta: Leiden's Rapenburg three days after a powder ship exploded on 12 January 1807, painted by Johannes Jelgerhuis.
about: This is a view of the Rapenburg in Leiden three days after the powder ship exploded on 12 January 1807. Spectators and soldiers stand on the bridge in the foreground, a few men carry a victim away on a stretcher, and piled-up household goods lie at the right. The disaster happened at the Steenschuur, a canal near the Rapenburg. Johannes Jelgerhuis signed it as an actor of the Amsterdam theater, dated 15 January 1807.

meta: A family with a letter, a key, a candlestick and a marmot in an interior, painted by Caspar Netscher in 1649.
about: This is a family portrait in an interior, with the father and mother in the middle and two daughters and two sons around them. The father holds a letter and the mother a key, the boy at the left a candlestick, and the boy at the back sits at a table with books and writing materials. The girl at the right holds a marmot, and a little dog is in front. Two paintings hang on the back wall. Caspar Netscher painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1649.

meta: Maria Theresa, empress of Austria, in an enamel miniature by Jean-Étienne Liotard painted in Lyon in 1747.
about: Maria Theresa, who lived from 1717 to 1780, was empress of Austria and queen of Hungary and Bohemia. She is shown half-length, turned to the right. The Rijksmuseum includes it among its portrait miniatures despite its size because it is made in enamel. An inscription on the back says Liotard of Geneva painted it in Lyon in 1747.

meta: Isidore Pils's study of a reclining nude of about 1841, reminiscent of Ingres's odalisques, left partly blank.
about: The languorous pose of this woman recalls Ingres's popular paintings of odalisques, female slaves and concubines in Turkish harems. Much of the canvas is thinly painted or blank, which suggests a figure study, not a finished work. The French Academy in the 1800s saw the nude as the ultimate test of an artist's skill, and since models changed poses often, students had to work fast and plainly. Isidore Pils made it around 1841.
credit_line: Gift of Leonard C. Hanna Jr.

meta: A pair of trophies for the crafts of the cabinetmaker and the carpenter, designed by Jean-Charles Delafosse, about 1760.
about: At the left are tools, a drawing book and an oval relief of a beaver gnawing a pole, hung from a windlass. At the right are tools, drawings, a framed compass, a carpenter's rule and a snake, hung from a ribbon. Together they refer to the crafts of the cabinetmaker and the carpenter. Jean-Charles Delafosse made the design around 1760.

meta: Sequoyah, the Cherokee silversmith who devised a written alphabet, painted by Henry Inman.
about: Sequoyah was the son of a Cherokee woman and a Virginia fur trader, and he was a warrior, hunter and silversmith. He worked for twelve years to devise a way of writing the Cherokee language. His syllabary, with eighty-six symbols for the language's syllables, was approved by the Cherokee chiefs in 1825. It made possible a rapid spread of literacy through the Cherokee Nation. Henry Inman painted his portrait.

meta: Franz Liszt painted by Henri Lehmann in 1839, shortly before Lisztomania took hold.
about: Henri Lehmann painted this portrait of the composer and pianist Franz Liszt in 1839, not long before Lisztomania took hold and his concerts drew fanatical fans. Both men were in Italy. Liszt sat at the Villa Massimiliana in Lucca, but the work was finished in Rome. It was shown at the Salon of 1840 at the Louvre.
